content:
kevin: Quick status — ran a fast quant smoke on kyros-11b int6 (w/ O2 int6 config). Results look promising on tokens/sec and token cost, but we see a small recall regression on long-form QA slices. Sending numbers below.
lina: can you paste the slice that regressed? wanted to check prompt fragility.
kevin: pasted a representative failed case, see below. Also perf:
```
throughput: 650 tok/s (baseline float16: 420 tok/s)
avg latency: 110ms -> 72ms
unit_cost_per_1k_tokens: $0.0026 -> $0.0017 (approx -35%)
quality_delta (ROUGE-L paraphrase slices): -1.8% absolute
```
samir: -1.8% is nontrivial depending on slice. Is this concentrated on long-context >1024?
maria: checked -- it's mostly multi-turn summarization with heavy entity-copying. Short QA unaffected.
lina: Hmm ok. Do we have logits-level diffs or attention pattern changes?
kevin: quick logit diffs look like weaker probability mass on long entity spans. I dumped a token-by-token perplexity diff for that sample.
kevin: attaching short snippet: `ppl_float16=8.2, ppl_int6=9.6` on that sequence.
kevin: Also tried a bias-correction trick (rescale final-layer logits by +0.02 for entity tokens) — small improvement but noisy.
maria: Could we try hybrid routing: route long-form to float16 kyros-11b and short-form to int6? What's the unit-econ tradeoff?
samir: Rough calc: if 20% of traffic is long and we route those to float16, blended unit cost becomes 0.2*$0.0026 + 0.8*$0.0017 = $0.00188 (~-28% vs baseline). Latency for long queries stays higher but overall cost savings remain.
lina: That seems reasonable. Need to ensure throughput targets for long traffic on existing capacity. Ops-bot can we check headroom?
ops-bot: @eng-ml checking capacity for kyros-11b float16 pool... current headroom: 12% in us-west, 9% in eu-west. Predicted QPS uplift if 20% route to float16: +18% on float16 pool.
kevin: So we either reserve a small dedicated float16 slot for long queries or do smart overflow to float16 in another region.
maria: Also consider a selective fallback policy: prefer int6 but fallback to float16 on quality-signal threshold (e.g., hallucination score > 0.6 or token-entropy spike). That reduces routing complexity.
samir: Agree. We should add a quick eval slice run across 500 long-form examples with int6 + selective fallback to estimate blended quality. Could run in a couple hours.
lina: Action items: 1) kevin run 500-sample long-form sweep with fallback flag and post metrics (cost, ROUGE, hallucination) 2) ops run capacity sim for 20% long routing 3) maria bake a short product note on UX latency expectations.
kevin: I'll start sweep now and post results in this thread when ready. Will include per-slice deltas and recommended routing thresholds.
maria: Thanks — once we have the sweep, we'll draft routing+rollout plan for GTN. :thumbsup:
kevin: ETA ~3h. tagging @samir and @lina for any extra checks.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled smoke run job kyros-int6-sweep-1792223334 started (job id: jb-7842).
